frame_metadata.gps_note: First take with GPS on every frame. App frames carry a 9-key GPS block written by the F0 build; stock-camera HEICs carry Apple's full 15-key block. Both bind the frame to the Met to within a few metres.

source_note: App frames are camera-roll copies (Image Capture over USB) bound to the manifest by capture time with tools/manifest/bind-frames.py — see derived/2026-09-20-met-frames.json. f0030 (MWFU3479) is a misfire — floor and plinth, zero text. Kept as the negative case: the app accepted a label frame with no OCR result and let the tester shoot again; it did not warn.

expected.date_edtf_note: BCE years are astronomical: 375 BCE is -0374. Ranges are intervals; '~' marks each end when the label says 'ca.'. A named span like 'late 6th century' is written as the conventional interval and noted in date_raw. Two dates on one label: the copy's and the original's. The object's date is the copy's; the original's is a relationship to another thing.
expected.medium_note: Not on the label. API: 'Tempera on paper'.

differ.original_date: label 'ca. 1323–1295 BCE' vs API 'original ca. 1314–1300 BCE'. Reign dates for Haremhab differ by chronology; both are the Met's.
differ.title: label 'King Haremhab with Anubis (left) and Horus Son of Isis (right)' covers both objects; API 'The King with Anubis, Tomb of Haremhab' is one of them

traps.the_artist_is_the_copyist: Lancelot Crane painted the facsimile in 1910–11. He is the artist of accession 23.2.84 and has nothing to do with the tomb painting it copies. Attach him to the wrong node and the graph says a British painter worked in Dynasty 18.
traps.kv_57: '(KV 57)' — another parenthesised alphanumeric near the bottom of the tombstone block; Mac OCR read it 'KV S7'. Not an accession.
traps.section_header: 'Kings and Queens Meet the Gods' sits above the title in the same bold weight. A title extractor taking the first bold line gets the gallery section, not the object.
